reference_note: **P5 native hook-registration QA (not a new approved Claim):** A local logger `try/catch` does NOT attach an error handler to `on('tool.call', handler)`. The five unchanged original Codex/Sonnet observer candidates triggered `gating hook without .catch: tool.call` on exact CLI 2.1.302 even when native strict validation exited zero. First-party syntax is `on('tool.call', handler).catch(($ , e, next) => next(e))` for a transparent observer; `next(e)` in the recovery handler reuses the completed downstream result rather than duplicating tool execution. Source-hashed synthetic 302/303/304 tests: 9/9 warning-free strict validations and 18/18 stubbed result/denial checks, plus a deliberately result-withholding recovery rejected in all three versions. Keep inner logger `try/catch` to isolate diagnostic failures; the registration `.catch` is a separate protection. Do not apply pass-through recovery to security enforcement: a `tool.check` gate must deny on failure. This is narrow native evidence, not full host/API compatibility or an approved new Claim. First-party: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/events#handle-a-hook-that-fails.
